edges.description: Altered alpha-actinin-2 disrupts its structural cross-linking role at the Z-disk, degrading sarcomeric organization.
Protein-extending frameshift variants render alpha-actinin-2 aggregation-prone.
Aggregated alpha-actinin-2 and increased protein expression disrupt normal Z-line organization.
Progressive myofibrillar breakdown produces the histopathologic and clinical features of the distal myopathy.
edges.target: Distal skeletal muscle degeneration and weakness

evidence.reference_title: Protein-extending ACTN2 frameshift variants cause variable myopathy phenotypes by protein aggregation.
evidence.snippet: The primary function of alpha-actinin-2 is to link actin and titin to the sarcomere Z-disk.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation update for the ACTN2 gene.
evidence.snippet: ACTN2 encodes alpha-actinin-2, a protein expressed in human cardiac and skeletal muscle.

nodes.description: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in ACTN2 alter alpha-actinin-2, a sarcomeric Z-disk protein. Two dominant classes are recognized: missense variants (the original Spanish and Swedish actininopathy families) and single-nucleotide deletions in the last exon that shift the reading frame and append a novel, unstructured, slightly extended C-terminal sequence.

evidence.reference_title: Actininopathy: A new muscular dystrophy caused by ACTN2 dominant mutations.
evidence.snippet: In all 3 Spanish families, we identified a unique missense variant in the ACTN2 gene cosegregating with the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Out-of-Frame Mutations in ACTN2 Last Exon Cause a Dominant Distal Myopathy With Facial Weakness.
evidence.snippet: High-throughput sequencing identified in each proband a heterozygous single nucleotide deletion (c.2558del and c.2567del) in the last exon of the ACTN2 gene.

evidence.reference_title: Out-of-Frame Mutations in ACTN2 Last Exon Cause a Dominant Distal Myopathy With Facial Weakness.
evidence.snippet: The deletions are predicted to lead to a novel but unstructured slightly extended C-terminal amino acid sequence.

nodes.description: Dominant frameshift variants that extend the alpha-actinin-2 protein cause it to form intracellular aggregates in muscle-cell models, whereas recessive missense variants do not, implicating alpha-actinin-2 aggregation as the disease mechanism for this class of dominant actininopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Protein-extending ACTN2 frameshift variants cause variable myopathy phenotypes by protein aggregation.
evidence.snippet: Conversely, dominant frameshift variants causing a protein extension do form alpha-actinin-2 aggregates.

evidence.reference_title: Protein-extending ACTN2 frameshift variants cause variable myopathy phenotypes by protein aggregation.
evidence.snippet: The results suggest that alpha-actinin-2 aggregation is the disease mechanism underlying some dominant actininopathies, and thus, we recommend that protein-extending frameshift variants in ACTN2 should be classified as pathogenic.

nodes.description: Chronic myofibrillar degeneration is expressed histologically as internalized nuclei, myofibrillar disorganization, rimmed vacuoles, and in some families multi-minicores, and clinically as slowly progressive distal muscle weakness that begins in the anterior lower leg and later extends proximally.

evidence.reference_title: Out-of-Frame Mutations in ACTN2 Last Exon Cause a Dominant Distal Myopathy With Facial Weakness.
evidence.snippet: Muscle biopsy showed internalized nuclei, myofibrillar disorganization, and rimmed vacuoles.

nodes.description: Loss of normal alpha-actinin-2 Z-disk cross-linking, together with abnormal accumulation of the protein, produces disorganized Z-lines and myofibrillar disarray. Muscle-sample analysis shows increased alpha-actinin-2 expression and abnormal Z-line organization.

evidence.reference_title: A novel frameshift ACTN2 variant causes a rare adult-onset distal myopathy with multi-minicores.
evidence.snippet: functional analysis using muscle samples revealed that the variant significantly increased the expression level of α-actinin-2 and resulted in abnormal Z-line organization of muscle fiber.
